objective.primaryRule: No primary and no roles: nothing is searched for selection, ranked for a decision or selected (AD1). The study delivers the risk-envelope inputs through the official GpuPool/EvalLab interface (opt-in, backward compatible), centralizes the risk-envelope qualification logic, and — only if every gate passes (PROTOCOL.md section 6) — renews the GPU acceptance with a full checklist section 2 cycle. The risk-envelope pilot is prepared for review only and is not run (AD9).

risk.denominator: one fixed $100,000 principal budget (not peak account equity)

budget.notes: No search proposals for selection. backendEvaluations caps fresh CPU evaluations on real data (the CPU arms of the mini schedule, plain and with the envelope; the CPU references of the parity campaign, the finalists and the risk-delivery parity). GPU evaluations (sealed replays, the mini schedule, parity, reliability) are counted separately in the records; synthetic fixtures are not counted.

evaluationBackend.justification: Engineering acceptance study (GPU Phase 7): CPU evaluations are parity references (records and risk envelopes) and the non-official CPU arm of the mini schedule; GPU runs are non-official replays of sealed jobs, the mini schedule, parity and reliability tests. Nothing is official optimization evidence (standard 3.0.0 section 9.8); the engineering output, if every gate passes, is a new acceptance record (section 9.9) for the final code.

chronologicalConsequence: not applicable: a diagnostic with no search for selection and no chronological verdict (AD2)

deviations.description: no roles and no primary; nothing is selected
deviations.justification: brief: engineering assignment; no trading-rule, fitness, search or selection change

deviations.description: no search for selection, no chronological verdict; sealed jobs of Assignments 3 and 2 replayed with their own frozen code and seeds (Assignment 3 C19 broad1 also with the risk envelope requested), and the parity-only mini schedule, compared by identity only
deviations.justification: brief Phase F: sealed historical candidate reproduction, fixed-seed mini-optimizer parity as engineering verification only

deviations.description: development doors D19-D24 and the parity windows; FULL and the 2025 window only inside the parity campaign identity comparisons (no figure reported); two compressed Assignment 3 search archives restored read-only to a scratch directory for threshold-edge subjects and the sealed-archive reproduction check
deviations.justification: brief sections 2.1, 4 and 8: verify the restored archives; threshold-edge parity; every door of the parity checklist

deviations.description: the CPU engine is the unmodified canonical reference (no file of the CPU closure is edited); every result of the final path must reproduce the canonical or sealed records bit for bit
deviations.justification: brief: no change of trading algorithms, numerical formulas, the CPU engine or the CUDA algorithms; every result must reproduce the canonical or sealed records bit for bit

deviations.description: not applicable: no fold primary or final candidate
no tuning benchmark: batch size and host workers stay Phase 4 decisions; timings are reported (the pilot compute estimate), never decision inputs
stricter: no money figure of a searched configuration is reported as a finding; the one failing parity candidate's record appears only as diagnostic evidence of field identity
deviations.justification: brief: no new trading candidate is optimized here

deviations.description: bounded reliability (two concurrent processes x 32 minutes) instead of an endurance test
deviations.justification: brief Phase F: bounded reliability testing

deviations.description: the risk-envelope pilot is prepared for review only (research/vg-l0-risk-envelope-pilot/PROTOCOL_PROPOSED.md): no pilot job, adoption, preflight, attestation or search is created or run, and no standard change is made
deviations.justification: brief: stop before executing the pilot; the user reviews and authorizes separately (the user instructions take precedence, section 0.4)
